tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

319	- 445 au texte inchangé ;
320	- 7 réécrits ;
321	- 3 retirés.
322	
323	### Énoncés retirés (3)
324	
325	| Passe 5 | Remplacé par | Raison |
326	|---|---|---|
327	| `nested_same_value` | — (cas `na4`) | F1 : la valeur arène est le détenteur de `internal`. Une arène imbriquée dont le bloc est émis vers une autre valeur a une autre valeur arène ; l'énoncé est faux. |
328	| `staticPinnedBottom_not_invariant` | `staticPinnedBottom_excludes_owned_static` | F3 : sa première conjonction (l'obligation vaut sur l'état initial de `stO`) est fausse sous la possession directe. Le nouveau théorème énonce cette négation et garde les deux autres faits (atteignabilité de `o3`, sortie rejetée). |
329	| `OwnedStorage.of_P` | — | F2 : `OwnedStorage` est retiré. |
330	
331	### Énoncés réécrits (7)
332	
333	| Énoncé | Changement | Raison |
334	|---|---|---|
335	| `newArena_det`, `newArena_preserves` | `NewArenaStep st` → `NewArenaStep st i` | F1 : `internal` nommée par l'appelant ; sens inchangé. |
336	| `arenaInv_transport` | hypothèses sur le détenteur de `internal` (un emplacement) et la longueur de `P`, au lieu de la possession du stockage | F1, F2 ; lemme auxiliaire. La conjonction sur l'origine absente, inutilisée depuis D3, est retirée. |
337	| `arena_dies_with_internal` | hypothèse `ArenaInv s ar` retirée | F1 ; énoncé renforcé, (c) 13. |
338	| `releaseEff_eq` | l'effet sur `D` est ajouté | F4. |
339	| `enter_not_inv3_preserving`, `alloc_not_inv3_preserving` | état témoin avec `callParams` | champ de `S3` (F6) ; sens inchangé. |
340	
341	**Sens nouveau des définitions, à texte inchangé.**
342	- **`S3`** reçoit `callParams`, que les énoncés ne lisent pas, hors F6.
343	- **`ArenaInv`** change de clauses ((c) 2). Il est plus faible pour la possession du stockage (un emplacement existant suffit) et l'est aussi pour le détenteur de `internal` : un emplacement quelconque, et non plus le propriétaire du stockage. Les énoncés qui le supposent valent sur plus d'états : `arena_issue_preserves_disjointness`, `arena_issue_keeps_earlier_blocks`, `arena_reset_rejects_live_issued`, `arena_reset_preserves`, `arena_reuse_safe`, `issue_disjoint_redundant`, `arena_entry_follows_transfer`, `arena_inv_preserved`. Ceux qui le concluent concluent moins, comme F1 et F2 l'imposent.
344	- **`arenaValue`** lit le détenteur de `internal`. `arena_entry_follows_transfer` parle maintenant du transfert de la valeur qui détient `internal`.
345	- **`StaticPinnedBottom`** est plus fort (possession directe). `static_pinned_never_exits` vaut sur moins d'états, comme F3 l'impose.
346	- **`ReleasePre`** est plus faible (clause 3, (c) 6) et `releaseEff` modifie `D`. Les théorèmes sur `release` (`release_preserves`, `release_preserves_anchorOrder`, `release_preserves_noDangling`, `release_restores_authority`, `release_releases`) valent pour plus de pas.
347	- **`KStep` et `Reachable`** reçoivent `store` ; `Reachable` prend le nouveau `newArena`. Voir (o).
348	
349	Hormis `arenaInv_transport`, lemme auxiliaire dont les hypothèses suivent F1 et F2, et le retrait d'une hypothèse (renforcement) dans `arena_dies_with_internal`, aucune hypothèse n'est ajoutée à un énoncé de la passe 5.
350	
351	## (j) Transfert, fin d'usage et allocation des valeurs composites
352	
353	La description de la passe 5 ((j)) vaut, avec ces ajouts.
354	
355	- **`store a p`.**
356	  - `a`, dérivée et détenue par le cadre courant, devient détenue par `p` et ancre de `p` ; les feuilles de `p` deviennent `Init`.
357	  - Écrire dans un champ ancre le champ ; le conteneur hérite de l'ancre par `depsOf` (MM-03.3.6).
358	- **Transfert d'une valeur qui contient une autorité stockée.**
359	  - L'autorité suit la valeur : détentrice dans la source ou une de ses parties (A4), elle devient détenue par la destination, et son ancre suit (`depsOf`).
360	  - Vers un cadre plus ancien que celui de son ancre effective, le transfert est rejeté (`store_escape_rejected_at_transfer`).
361	- **`release` d'une autorité stockée.** Il exige `Modify` exerçable sur son emplacement (C4) et la retire de ses ancres (F4).
362	- **`endUse` d'une valeur qui contient une autorité stockée.** L'autorité est libérée (A6), ses ancres supprimées.
363	- **`endUse` d'une valeur qui détient l'origine d'une autorité stockée ailleurs.** Il est rejeté tant que l'autorité stockée vit (cas s7).
364	- **Arène.**
365	  - Sa valeur est le détenteur de `internal`. Le transfert de cette valeur emporte l'arène ; son `endUse` la finit.
366	  - Le stockage peut être un local, un statique, une racine allouée ou un bloc (F2).
367	
368	## (k) Obligations de sûreté des contrats `K`
369	
370	Inchangées (passe 5, (k)), sauf **`Pinned`** : `StaticPinnedBottom` exige maintenant la possession directe par le cadre de base (F3). Elle exclut l'état initial de `stO`, où le statique épinglé appartient à un autre statique (`staticPinnedBottom_excludes_owned_static`).
371	
372	## (l) Cas de fuite rencontrés
373	
374	Ceux de la passe 5 ((l)), plus le cycle de F7 (a) : deux autorités stockées, chacune exerçable seulement par l'autre, ne peuvent être libérées par aucun pas essayé dans l'état `fa8`. Elles bloquent l'`endUse` des valeurs de nœud et le `reset`, jusqu'à la sortie du cadre, qui les libère. Ce n'est pas une fuite de stockage, mais une ressource de l'arène retenue jusqu'à la sortie ; voir (p).
375	
376	## (m) Statut de `exitFrame_no_dangling`
377	
378	Inchangé (passe 5, (m)). `exitFrame_no_dangling_reachable` porte sur le nouveau `Reachable`.
379	
380	## (n) Bilan de clôture du jalon 1
381	
382	### 1. Sûreté démontrée du noyau abstrait séquentiel sur les états atteints
383	
384	`Reachable k statics` est la clôture de `S3.init statics`, pour un stockage statique valide, par dix-neuf opérations :
385	- les seize du noyau : `derive`, `split`, `release`, `transfer`, `depend`, `enterFrame`, `exitFrame`, `read3`, `write3`, `writeShared`, `pin`, `unpin`, `endUse`, `free`, `alloc`, `store` ;
386	- les trois de l'arène : `newArena`, `issue`, `reset`.
387	
388	Seule hypothèse sur `K` : `DDSound k`.
389	
390	**Invariants des états atteints** (`reachable_access_invariant_underDD`) : `WF3 s ∧ Inv3 s ∧ ∀ ar ∈ s.arenas, s.Active ar.internal → ArenaInv s ar`, avec :
391	- `WF3` (A1, A4, B1, C3) : la bonne formation de la passe 5, `RootHeld` inchangé ;
392	- `Inv3 = Inv3base ∧ AnchorOrder ∧ NoDangling` (MM-03.3 §2, B8, C1, C2) ;
393	- pour toute arène vivante, `ArenaInv` (§6, A10, F1, F2) :
394	  - régions émises et disponibles dans le stockage ;
395	  - régions émises simultanément valides deux à deux disjointes, et disjointes des régions disponibles ;
396	  - chaque émission est un bloc `Modify` dérivé de `internal` ;
397	  - le stockage est un emplacement ;
398	  - `internal` est `Modify`, détenue par un emplacement, la valeur arène, et couvre exactement le stockage.
399	
400	**Préservation.**
401	- Pour `WF3 ∧ Inv3`, le tableau de la passe 5, plus `store` : `store_preserves`, `store_preserves_anchorOrder`, `store_preserves_noDangling`.
402	- Pour les arènes : `kstep_preserves_arenas` (dont `store`), `newArena_preserves`, `issueAt_preserves`, `resetAt_preserves`.
403	
404	**Conséquences démontrées.**
405	- Celles de la passe 5, (n) 1, sur le nouveau domaine.
406	- `live_arena_storage_usable`.
407	- `store_root_rejected` ; `store_escape_rejected_at_transfer`.
408	- `transfer_footprints_disjoint` ; `transfer_overlap_redundant`.
409	- `call_params_effective_protected`.
410	
411	**Limites.**
412	- La sûreté porte sur les accès ; rien n'est dit des valeurs, de la terminaison, ni du progrès : F7 (a) montre un blocage jusqu'à la sortie de cadre.
413	- Les verdicts des cas valent pour leurs états concrets.
414	- F6 n'est pas démontrable tel qu'énoncé ((d) 1).
415	- L'échappement d'un bloc émis n'est rejeté qu'à la sortie du cadre ((d) 3).
416	
417	### 2. Propriétés conditionnées aux contrats `K`
418	
419	Le tableau de la passe 5, (n) 2, vaut. Changement : `StaticPinnedBottom` porte sur la possession directe (F3).
420	
421	### 3. Ce que le raffinement vers MM-02 (jalon 2) doit établir
422	
423	La liste de la passe 5, (n) 3, vaut. S'y ajoutent :
424	1. **`store`.** L'écriture d'une référence est une écriture de MM-02 dans les feuilles de `p`. Sa correspondance avec un pointeur réel est à établir.
425	2. **Arène sur un stockage quelconque (F2).** Un stockage local ou statique d'arène correspond à une sous-région d'une allocation de MM-02 (pile ou statique). L'écriture des métadonnées correspond à une écriture réelle dans la valeur arène, détentrice de `internal`.
426	
427	### 4. Ce qui reste hors périmètre
428	
429	Inchangé (passe 5, (n) 4). S'y ajoutent, par la tâche : pool de handles, flot de contrôle, suspension, corpus MM3-H complet (jalon 3). Les pointeurs bruts sont hors du noyau (F6).
430	
431	## (o) Énoncés de (n) 1 qui changent de domaine
432	
433	| Énoncé de (n) 1 | Changement de domaine |
434	|---|---|
435	| `reachable_access_invariant_underDD`, `reachable_invariants`, `reachable_no_dangling`, `exitFrame_no_dangling_reachable` | `Reachable` compte le pas `store`, et `newArena` prend une `internal` nommée par l'appelant (F1) : plus d'arènes (stockage local, statique, bloc ; plusieurs arènes sur les mêmes feuilles avec des `internal` différentes). La conclusion porte sur le nouvel `ArenaInv` ((i)). |
436	| énoncés qui supposent `ArenaInv` (`arena_issue_preserves_disjointness`, `arena_issue_keeps_earlier_blocks`, `arena_reset_rejects_live_issued`, `arena_reset_preserves`, `arena_reuse_safe`, `issue_disjoint_redundant`, `arena_entry_follows_transfer`, `arena_inv_preserved`) | plus d'états ((i)) |
437	| énoncés sur `release` (`release_preserves`, `release_preserves_anchorOrder`, `release_preserves_noDangling`, `release_restores_authority`) | plus de pas : la clause 3 de `ReleasePre` est plus faible ; l'effet retire une ancre (F4) |
438	| `static_pinned_never_exits` | moins d'états : obligation plus forte (F3) |
439	| les énoncés sur tout état (`write3_exclusive`, `effective_exclusive`, `transfer_*`, `free_no_dangling`, `*_det`…) | le type `S3` a un champ de plus, qu'ils ne lisent pas ; `KStep` a un constructeur de plus, que `arena_inv_preserved`, `KStep.arenas` et `KStep.active_back` couvrent |
440	
441	## (p) Résultats de F7
442	
443	### F7 (a) : cycle sur nœuds entiers
444	
445	Construit depuis `S3.init []` par des pas de `Reachable` (`progress_cycle_whole_nodes`).
446	
447	**Mise en place.**
448	- Cadre 1 : 0 valeur arène, 1 allocateur, 2 et 3 valeurs de nœud.
449	- `alloc` donne le stockage 4, de parties A = 5 et B = 6, possédé par 0, de racine 4 détenue par 0.
450	- `newArena 4 4`.
451	- Les blocs 5 (`[5]`) et 6 (`[6]`) sont émis vers 2 et 3.
452	
453	| Pas | Attendu | Obtenu |
454	|---|---|---|
455	| `derive 6 6 Modify` (vue sur B depuis le bloc de B), autorité 7 | — | `ok` |
456	| `store 7 5` (dans A) | `ok` | `ok` |
457	| `derive 5 5 Modify` (vue sur A depuis le bloc de A), autorité 8 | — | `ok` |
458	| `store 8 6` (dans B), état `fa7` | `reject` | **`ok`** |
459	
460	**Pas en cause et clause : `store 8 6` dans `fa7`.** Aucune clause de `StorePre` n'échoue. La seule qui pourrait rejeter est « `Modify` exerçable sur `p` » (`HasRight s .modify 6`), et elle est vraie :
461	- dans `fa7`, le bloc 6 a perdu son `Modify` effectif sur B au profit de 7 ;
462	- mais 7, détenue par A, est exerçable par la règle des autorités détenues (A2, B2), au moyen de 8, détenue par le cadre et de `Modify` effectif sur A ;
463	- 7 a donc `Modify` effectif sur B.
464	
465	Après le pas, 7 n'est plus exerçable que par 8, détenue par B, et 8 que par 7, détenue par A : aucune n'est exerçable (énoncé au mode `Observe`).
466	
467	**Dans `fa8`, ces pas sont rejetés :**
468	- `release 7` et `release 8` (C4 : pas de `Modify` exerçable sur A ni sur B) ;
469	- `endUse` de 2 et de 3 (A6, O3.2 : un descendant actif d'un bloc libéré est détenu ailleurs) ;
470	- `reset` (A10 : des blocs dérivés de `internal` sont actifs).
471	
472	Les rejets de `endUse` et de `reset` existent déjà avant le second `store`, où 8 pouvait encore être libérée d'abord. La sortie du cadre 1 est acceptée et libère 7 et 8. Qu'une autre séquence libère 7 ou 8 avant la sortie reste un résultat ouvert : aucune impossibilité n'est démontrée. Question (e) 2.
473	
474	### F7 (b) : cycle sur champs disjoints
475	
476	Construit depuis `S3.init []` par des pas de `Reachable` (`progress_cycle_disjoint_fields`).
477	
478	**Mise en place.**
479	- Stockage 4, de nœuds A = 5 (champs `data` = 6, `link` = 7) et B = 8 (`data` = 9, `link` = 10).
480	- Les blocs 5 (`[6, 7]`) et 6 (`[9, 10]`) sont émis vers 2 et 3.
481	
482	| Pas | Attendu | Obtenu |
483	|---|---|---|
484	| `derive 6 9 Modify` (vue sur `B.data`), autorité 7 ; `store 7 7` (dans `A.link`) | `ok` | `ok` |
485	| `derive 5 6 Modify` (vue sur `A.data`), autorité 8 ; `store 8 10` (dans `B.link`) | `ok` | `ok` |
486	| `release 7` ; `release 8` | `ok` | `ok`, chacune quittant les ancres de son champ |
487	| `endUse 2` ; `endUse 3` (valeurs de nœud) | `ok` | `ok`, les blocs libérés |
488	| `reset` de l'arène | `ok` | `ok` |
489	
490	Démontage : `release 7`, `release 8`, `endUse 2`, `endUse 3`, `reset`. Le théorème énonce la liste d'arènes non vide après les deux `store` et avant le `reset`.
491	
492	Avec l'autre lecture de « `endUse` des nœuds » (les parties 5 et 8 du stockage, (c) 10), la séquence de la tâche est rejetée au premier `endUse` : `EndUseAccessOK` (A6, O3.2), le bloc 5, détenu par la valeur vivante 2, couvrant les feuilles finissantes. La séquence plus longue `release` des blocs 5 et 6, `endUse 5`, `endUse 8`, `reset` est acceptée (vérifiée par la revue, hors module). Question (e) 5.

/-- `store_escape_rejected_at_transfer` (F4; MM-03.3.1: « Un accès temporaire ne peut être
prolongé simplement en le stockant dans un cadre plus ancien »; MM-03.3.6; C1): a value `src`,
one of whose parts (`src` included) is anchored on an authority `a` whose effective anchor is
held by the current frame `f`, such as an authority derived from a local of `f` and stored into
`src` or one of its fields, cannot be transferred to a destination whose frame, after the
transfer, is an older frame `g`: the dependency follows the value (`depsOf`, MM-03.3.6;
MM-03.3 §3, O4) and the clause B8 of `transfer` checks its effective anchor. It speaks of the
authorities placed by `store`, which anchors them; a block issued to `src` is held without being
an anchor (pass-6 report, (d)). -/
theorem store_escape_rejected_at_transfer {k : K} {s : S3} {src dst a f g : Nat} {F₀ : Frames}
    {z : Authority} (hwf : WF3 s) (hF : s.F = f :: F₀) (ha : a ∈ depsOf s src)
    (hz : s.A[s.effAnchor a]? = some z) (hzf : z.holder = .frame f)
    (hg : (transferEff s src dst).pframe dst = some g) (hgF : g ∈ F₀) :
    TransferStep k src dst s .reject := by
  refine .reject fun hpre => ?_
  have hdst : (transferEff s src dst).Usable dst := hpre.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.1
  have hin : a ∈ (transferEff s src dst).D dst := by

/-! ## Redundant preconditions (A11) -/

/-- O1.4 follows from O1.1 and O1.3 under I1 (MM-03.3 §3, O1; A11): it is not a precondition of
`derive`. -/
theorem derive_compat_redundant {s : S3} {src q : Nat} {m : Mode} (h1 : I1 s) (hs : s.Active src)
    (h3 : ∀ p ∈ footprint s.P q, Allows (effective s src p) m) : DeriveCompat s src q m := by
  obtain ⟨x, hx, -⟩ := hs
  have hI := addAuth_I1 (hd := .frame s.top) h1 hx h3
  intro b hb p hpq
  have hn : effective (deriveEff s src q m) s.A.length p = some m := by

def S3.afp (s : S3) (a : Nat) : List Nat := match s.A[a]? with
  | some x => x.footprint
  | none => []

/-- Appends an authority to `A`: its identity is `s.A.length`. -/
def S3.addAuth (s : S3) (y : Authority) : S3 := { s with A := s.A ++ [y] }

/-- Anchors of the value at `q`, inherited from its parts (MM-03.3.6: a containing value
inherits the dependencies of the contained values). -/
def depsOf (s : S3) (q : Nat) : List Nat :=
  ((List.range s.P.length).filter fun r => decide (partOf s.P r q)).flatMap s.D

/-- Dependencies still valid for the values containing leaf `p` (MM-03.3 §5): every anchor of a
place of which `p` is a part is active. -/
def DepsValid (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, partOf s.P p q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, s.Active x

instance (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Decidable (DepsValid s p) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (∀ _ ∈ _, _))

/-- Non-escape restriction (MM-03.3.6) for anchor `x` and a destination of frame `fd`: if `x`
is a local anchor (no origin), its frame is `fd` or an ancestor of it, so `fd` does not outlive
it. The frame of an anchor is the frame of its holder (A4, A5). -/
def NoEscape (s : S3) (x : Nat) (fd : Option Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[x]?) (fun y => y.origin = none →
    OptP (s.hframe y.holder) (fun g => OptP fd (fun f => ancestor s.F g f) True) True) True

instance (s : S3) (x : Nat) (fd : Option Nat) : Decidable (NoEscape s x fd) := by
  unfold NoEscape; infer_instance

/-- C1: the frame of the effective anchor of `x` exists and is `fd`, the frame of the dependent,
or one of its ancestors (MM-03.3.1, `ancestor`). The frame of an authority is the frame of its
holder (A4, A5). -/
def EffAnchorOK (s : S3) (x : Nat) (fd : Option Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[s.effAnchor x]?) (fun z => OptP (s.hframe z.holder)
    (fun g => OptP fd (fun f => ancestor s.F g f) False) False) False

instance (s : S3) (x : Nat) (fd : Option Nat) : Decidable (EffAnchorOK s x fd) := by
  unfold EffAnchorOK; infer_instance

/-- `mapI f i l` applies `f` to each element of `l` with its index, counted from `i`. -/
def mapI {α β : Type} (f : Nat → α → β) : Nat → List α → List β
  | _, [] => []
  | i, a :: l => f i a :: mapI f (i + 1) l

theorem length_mapI {α β : Type} (f : Nat → α → β) :
    ∀ (i : Nat) (l : List α), (mapI f i l).length = l.length
  | _, [] => rfl
  | i, _ :: l => by simp [mapI, length_mapI f (i + 1) l]

theorem getElem?_mapI {α β : Type} (f : Nat → α → β) :
    ∀ (i : Nat) (l : List α) (j : Nat), (mapI f i l)[j]? = (l[j]?).map (f (i + j))
  | _, [], _ => rfl
  | i, a :: l, 0 => by simp [mapI]
  | i, a :: l, j + 1 => by
    simp only [mapI, List.getElem?_cons_succ, getElem?_mapI f (i + 1) l j]
    congr 2; omega

/-! ## Exercisable authorities (A2, B2) -/

/-- `s.ExercisableAt a m` (B2): authority `a` is exercisable at mode `m` when `m` does not exceed its
----
instance (P : List Place) (q : Nat) (h : Holder) : Decidable (heldIn P q h) := by
  cases h <;> unfold heldIn <;> infer_instance

/-- Effect of `transfer(source, destination)` (MM-03.3 §3, O4; A4; A5): the destination becomes
`Init`, the source `Moved`; the anchors of the source, inherited ones included, join those of
the destination and leave the source and its parts; every authority held by the source or one
of its parts is now held by the destination (A4); every place owned by the source or one of its
parts is now owned by the destination, without moving (A5). -/
def transferEff (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) : S3 :=
  { s with
    P := s.P.map fun pl => if heldIn s.P src pl.owner then { pl with owner := .place dst } else pl
    I := fun l => if l ∈ footprint s.P dst then .init
      else if l ∈ footprint s.P src then .moved else s.I l
    D := fun q => if q = dst then s.D dst ++ depsOf s src
      else if partOf s.P q src then [] else s.D q
    A := s.A.map fun y => if heldIn s.P src y.holder then { y with holder := .place dst } else y }

/-- Active derived access covering a leaf of the source and not moved with it
(MM-03.3 §3, O4.4; A4). -/
def ActiveDerivedOutside (s : S3) (src j : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ y.origin ≠ none ∧ ¬ heldIn s.P src y.holder ∧
----

instance (s : S3) (src x : Nat) : Decidable (AnchorMoves s src x) := by
  unfold AnchorMoves; infer_instance

/-- Anchors of the places whose frame changes when the value at `src` is transferred (A5;
MM-03.3.6): `src`, its parts, and the usable places it owns, transitively. An anchor of a dead
owned place is not read: no usable place depends on it (MM-03.3.6). -/
def movedDeps (s : S3) (src : Nat) : List Nat :=
  ((List.range s.P.length).filter fun q =>
    decide (partOf s.P q src ∨ (OwnedWithin s src q ∧ s.Usable q))).flatMap s.D

/-- Preconditions of `transfer` (MM-03.3 §3, O4), in order: source usable (MM-03.3.1) and
1 initialised; 2 destination usable, without an `Init` leaf, sharing no leaf with the source (F5:
the footprints of source and destination are disjoint, the clause `¬ overlap`, redundant with
clauses 1 and 2 by `transfer_overlap_redundant`),
and still usable once it owns the source's storage (no ownership cycle); exercisable `Modify`
on the source and on the destination (B2); 4 no active derived
access on the source other than those it holds; 5 anchors of the value valid; 6 non-escape
(MM-03.3.6) towards the destination's frame, for the anchors of the value and of the usable
places it owns, whose frame changes with it (A5), each frame read after the transfer (B7);
7 no leaf of the source pinned, statically
(`Pinned`, MM-03.3.8) or dynamically (A8); B8 on the effective anchor (C1): for every dependent
usable after the transfer, if its effective anchor moves with the value, or if the dependent
itself moves (the destination, or a place the value owns), the frame of the effective anchor is
the dependent's frame or an ancestor of it, both frames read after the transfer
(`EffAnchorOK`). O4.3 holds by construction. -/
def TransferPre (k : K) (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  s.Usable src ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, s.I l = .init) ∧
  s.Usable dst ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init) ∧ ¬ overlap s.P src dst ∧
  HasRight s .modify src ∧ HasRight s .modify dst ∧
  (transferEff s src dst).Usable dst ∧
  (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, ¬ ActiveDerivedOutside s src j) ∧
  (∀ x ∈ depsOf s src, s.Active x) ∧
  (∀ x ∈ movedDeps s src,
    NoEscape (transferEff s src dst) x ((transferEff s src dst).pframe dst)) ∧
  (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, ¬ k.Pinned l ∧ s.pin l = false) ∧
  (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (transferEff s src dst).Usable q →
    ∀ x ∈ (transferEff s src dst).D q,
      (AnchorMoves s src (s.effAnchor x) ∨ q = dst ∨ OwnedWithin s src q) →
      EffAnchorOK (transferEff s src dst) x ((transferEff s src dst).pframe q))

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) :
    Decidable (TransferPre k s src dst) := by
  unfold TransferPre; infer_instance

/-- `transfer` as a relation (MM-03.3 §3, O4). -/
def TransferStep (k : K) (src dst : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (TransferPre k s src dst) (transferEff s src dst)

/-! ## O5 `depend` (MM-03.3 §3) -/

/-- Effect of `depend(result, anchor)` (MM-03.3 §3, O5): the anchor joins the dependencies of
the result place; existing dependencies are kept; propagation to containing values is computed
by `depsOf`. -/
def dependEff (s : S3) (q x : Nat) : S3 :=
  { s with D := fun r => if r = q then s.D q ++ [x] else s.D r }

/-- Preconditions of `depend` (MM-03.3 §3, O5), in order: result place usable (MM-03.3.1);
1 valid anchor; 5 non-escape (MM-03.3.6); B3: exercisable `Modify` on the result; C1: the frame
of the effective anchor is the frame of the result or an ancestor of it (`EffAnchorOK`). O5.2
(real origin of the rights or storage) is not representable: the state does not relate a value
to the origin of its content. O5.3 and O5.4 hold by construction. -/
def DependPre (s : S3) (q x : Nat) : Prop :=
  s.Usable q ∧ s.Active x ∧ NoEscape s x (s.pframe q) ∧ HasRight s .modify q ∧
    EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q)

instance (s : S3) (q x : Nat) : Decidable (DependPre s q x) := by
  unfold DependPre; infer_instance

/-- `depend` as a relation (MM-03.3 §3, O5). -/
def DependStep (q x : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (DependPre s q x) (dependEff s q x)

/-! ## F4 `store` -/

/-- Effect of `store a p` (F4), the write of a reference into a value: `a` is now held by the
place `p`; `a` joins the anchors of `p`; the leaves of `p` become `Init`. -/
def storeEff (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : S3 := match s.A[a]? with
  | some y => { s with
      A := s.A.set a { y with holder := .place p }
      D := fun q => if q = p then s.D p ++ [a] else s.D q
      I := fun l => if l ∈ footprint s.P p then .init else s.I l }
  | none => s

/-- Preconditions of `store a p` (F4), in order: `a` active, derived (`a.origin ≠ none`), held by
the current frame; `p` usable; exercisable `Modify` on `p` (B2, `HasRight`); `a` covers no leaf
of `p` nor of its owned storage, transitively (A5, `OwnedIn`); `AnchorOrder` for the added
anchor (C1, `EffAnchorOK`): the frame of the effective anchor of `a` is the frame of `p` or one
of its ancestors. No inverse operation exists (F4). -/
def StorePre (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[a]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ y.origin ≠ none ∧ y.holder = .frame s.top) False ∧
  s.Usable p ∧ HasRight s .modify p ∧
  (∀ l ∈ s.afp a, l ∉ footprint s.P p ∧
    ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, OwnedIn s.P p q → l ∉ footprint s.P q) ∧
  EffAnchorOK s a (s.pframe p)

instance (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : Decidable (StorePre s a p) := by unfold StorePre; infer_instance

/-- `store` as a relation (F4). -/
def StoreStep (a p : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (StorePre s a p) (storeEff s a p)

/-! ## O6 `enterFrame` (MM-03.3 §4, A5) -/

/-- Owner of the local of index `i` of `ls` (parent, owning local, kind) in the new frame `f`:
the owning local if any, the new frame otherwise (A5). -/
def localOwner (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) (f i : Nat) : Holder :=
  match (ls[i]?).bind (·.2.1) with
  | some o => .place o
  | none => .frame f

/-- Places after `enterFrame`: the locals `ls` appended, owned by the new frame `nF` or by an
earlier local (A5). -/
def enterP (s : S3) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : List Place :=
  s.P ++ (List.range ls.length).map fun i =>
    ⟨(ls[i]?).bind (·.1), localOwner ls s.nF i, ((ls[i]?).map (·.2.2)).getD 0⟩

/-- Indices, relative to `ls`, of the root locals (no parent). -/
def rootIdx (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : List Nat :=
  (List.range ls.length).filter fun i => ((ls[i]?).bind (·.1)).isNone

/-- Effect of `enterFrame` (MM-03.3 §4, O6) with parameters `ps` and locals `ls`: new frame
`nF` pushed; the parameters, derived by the caller, are now held by the new frame (A3); locals
appended, uninitialised, without dependency, alive and unpinned; one active root `Modify`
authority per root local on its footprint, held by the owner of the local (pass-1
arbitrage 2; A4); the ghost record `callParams` of the new frame is `ps` (F6). -/

/-! ### `store` of a root (F4) -/

/-- Frame 1: locals 0 and 1, of roots 0 and 1. Storing the root 0 into 1 is rejected (expected:

example : StoreStep 0 1 sr0 .reject :=

/-! ### `store`, then the end of the value that holds the origin (F4; A6) -/

/-- Frame 1: 0 value, 1 storage owned by 0, of root 1 held by 0, 2 another local. The frame
derives 3, `Modify` on 1, and stores it into 2. The `endUse` of 0, which releases the root 1, is
rejected (expected: reject): 3 descends from it and is held by 2 (A6; MM-03.3 §3, O3.2). After
the `release` of 3 (expected: `ok`; F4: 3 leaves the anchors of 2), the same `endUse` is accepted
(expected: `ok`). -/

def se1 : S3 := deriveEff se0 1 1 .modify
def se2 : S3 := storeEff se1 3 2

example : se2.D 2 = [3] := by decide

/-! ### `transfer(x, x.f)` (F5) -/

/-- Frame 1: 0 value `x` with the field 1, 2 a local `tmp`; the field is written. `transfer(x,
x.f)` is rejected (expected: reject): the footprints overlap (F5), and the destination is
initialised. Twin: `transfer(x.f, tmp)` then `transfer(tmp, x)` (expected: `ok`, `ok`). -/
def tx0 : S3 := write3Eff (enter1 [(none, none, 0), (some 0, none, 0), (none, none, 0)]) [1]
example : TransferStep K0 0 1 tx0 .reject := .reject (by decide)

/-! ### Non-vacuity of F6 -/

/-- Frame 1: local 0, of root 0; it derives 1, `Modify` on 0, and calls with `[1]`. In frame 2,
the root 0 of the caller covers the footprint of the parameter and is not exercisable by the
callee; `CallProtects` holds. After the callee releases the parameter (expected: `ok`), a write
or a read through the root and a derivation from it are rejected (expected: reject), and
`CallProtects` still holds. Two nested calls: frame 2 derives 2 from 1 and calls with `[2]`; in

after the exit of frame 2. In `pw0` the leaf is initialised before the call, so the rejected read

example : CallProtects pv1 := callProtects_of_check (by decide)
example : ReleaseStep 2 pv1 (.ok (releaseEff pv1 2)) := .ok (by decide)

example : Read3Step 1 [0] (write3Eff pv0 [0]) (.ok (write3Eff pv0 [0])) := .ok (by decide)

    (.ok (deriveEff (exitEff (releaseEff pv0 1)) 0 0 .modify)) := .ok (by decide)
example : Write3Step 2 [0] pv1 (.ok (write3Eff pv1 [0])) := .ok (by decide)

    (.ok (write3Eff (exitEff (releaseEff pv1 2)) [0])) := .ok (by decide)

    (.ok (write3Eff (exitEff (releaseEff (exitEff (releaseEff pv1 2)) 1)) [0])) := .ok (by decide)

/-! ### Progress (F7) -/

/-- F7 (a), cycle on whole nodes. Frame 1: 0 arena value, 1 allocator value, 2 and 3 node
values; storage 4 with the nodes 5 (A) and 6 (B), owned by 0, of root 4; `newArena 4 4`; the

def fa0 : S3 := enter1 [(none, none, 0), (none, none, 0), (none, none, 0), (none, none, 0)]
def fa1 : S3 :=
  allocEff (write3Eff fa0 [1]) 1 0 [(none, none, 0), (some 4, none, 0), (some 4, none, 0)]
def fa2 : S3 := newArenaEff fa1 4 4
def arFa : Arena := ⟨4, 4, [5, 6], []⟩

/-- `enterFrame` as a relation (MM-03.3 §4, O6; A3). -/
def EnterStep (ps : List Nat) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) (s : S3) :
    Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (EnterPre s ps ls) (enterEff s ps ls)

/-! ## O7 `exitFrame` (MM-03.3 §4, A4, A5, A7) -/

/-- Authority `x` survives the exit to stack `F₀`: active, and held by a holder still live once
the frame is popped, through transitive ownership (A4, A5). A7 speaks of an authority held by
a surviving frame; an authority held by a place is read as held by the frame that ends its
owner chain. -/
def Survives (s : S3) (F₀ : Frames) (x : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[x]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ HolderLive { s with F := F₀ } y.holder) False

instance (s : S3) (F₀ : Frames) (x : Nat) : Decidable (Survives s F₀ x) := by
  unfold Survives; infer_instance

/-- First surviving authority of a list (A7). -/
def firstSurv (s : S3) (F₀ : Frames) (l : List Nat) : Option Nat :=
  l.find? fun z => decide (Survives s F₀ z)

/-- Authority `a` after the exit (MM-03.3 §4, O7; A7): released unless it survives; a surviving
authority is re-attached to its first surviving strict ancestor along `origin`, which is its
origin when that origin survives. -/
def exitG (s : S3) (F₀ : Frames) (a : Nat) (y : Authority) : Authority :=
  if Survives s F₀ a then
    match y.origin with
    | none => y
    | some _ => { y with origin := firstSurv s F₀ (s.ancs a) }
  else { y with active := false }

/-- Preconditions of `exitFrame` (MM-03.3 §4, O7; A7; B4): the exiting frame has a caller; every
anchor of a place still usable after the exit has a surviving authority among itself and its
ancestors along `origin`; every surviving derived authority has a surviving strict ancestor;
B4: no leaf of a place that dies with the frame, transitively owned storage included, is
pinned, dynamically (A8) or statically (`Pinned`, MM-03.3.8). Otherwise the exit is rejected. -/
def ExitPre (k : K) (s : S3) : Prop :=
  match s.F with
  | _ :: F₀ => F₀ ≠ [] ∧
      (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, ({ s with F := F₀ } : S3).Usable q →
        ∀ x ∈ s.D q, firstSurv s F₀ (x :: s.ancs x) ≠ none) ∧
      (∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, Survives s F₀ a → s.org a ≠ none →
        firstSurv s F₀ (s.ancs a) ≠ none) ∧
      (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → ¬ ({ s with F := F₀ } : S3).Usable q →
        ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l)
  | [] => False

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) : Decidable (ExitPre k s) := by
  unfold ExitPre; split <;> infer_instance

/-- Effect of `exitFrame` (MM-03.3 §4, O7; A4; A5; A7): return to the caller; each anchor
replaced by the first surviving authority among itself and its ancestors; authorities that do
not survive released; surviving derived authorities re-attached. -/
def exitEff (s : S3) : S3 :=
  match s.F with
  | _ :: F₀ =>
    { s with
      F := F₀
      D := fun q => (s.D q).map fun x => (firstSurv s F₀ (x :: s.ancs x)).getD x
      A := mapI (exitG s F₀) 0 s.A }
  | [] => s

/-- `exitFrame` as a relation (MM-03.3 §4, O7). -/
def ExitStep (k : K) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop := Guarded (ExitPre k s) (exitEff s)

/-! ## Abstract reads and writes (MM-03.3 §5) -/

/-- Ordinary read condition of a leaf by authority `a` (MM-03.3 §5, `canRead3`): an effective
authority permits observation, the leaf is initialised, the needed dependencies are valid. The
type and storage contract is not represented. -/
def CanReadLeaf (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : Prop :=
  effective s a p ≠ none ∧ s.I p = .init ∧ DepsValid s p

instance (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : Decidable (CanReadLeaf s a p) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _))

/-- `canRead3` (MM-03.3 §5): ordinary read of leaves `ls` by authority `a`, exercisable at
`Observe` (B2). -/
def canRead3 (s : S3) (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) : Prop :=
  s.ExercisableAt a .observe ∧ ∀ p ∈ ls, CanReadLeaf s a p

instance (s : S3) (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) : Decidable (canRead3 s a ls) := by
  unfold canRead3; infer_instance

/-- `read3` as a relation (MM-03.3 §5): a read does not change the state. -/
def Read3Step (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (canRead3 s a ls) s

/-- `canWrite3` (MM-03.3 §5): `a` exercisable at `Modify` (B2); on each leaf, effective
`Modify` of `a` and needed dependencies valid. The clause "no other ordinary authority with an
incompatible effective right" is removed (A11): it follows from the first under I1
(`canWrite3_excl_redundant`). The type and storage condition is not represented. -/
def canWrite3 (s : S3) (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) : Prop :=
  s.ExercisableAt a .modify ∧ ∀ p ∈ ls, effective s a p = some .modify ∧ DepsValid s p

instance (s : S3) (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) : Decidable (canWrite3 s a ls) := by
  unfold canWrite3; infer_instance

/-- Effect of a write (MM-03.3 §5): written leaves become `Init`. -/
def write3Eff (s : S3) (ls : List Nat) : S3 := { s with I := fun p => if p ∈ ls then .init else s.I p }

/-- `write3` as a relation (MM-03.3 §5). -/
def Write3Step (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (canWrite3 s a ls) (write3Eff s ls)

/-! ## Lemmas on the effective authority (MM-03.3.5) -/

theorem effOf_cases {m m' : Mode} {ds : List Mode} (h : effOf m ds = some m') :
    (ds = [] ∧ m' = m) ∨ (ds ≠ [] ∧ Mode.modify ∉ ds ∧ m' = .observe) := by
  unfold effOf at h
  by_cases h0 : ds = []
  · simp [h0] at h; exact .inl ⟨h0, h.symm⟩
  · by_cases h1 : Mode.modify ∈ ds
    · simp [h0, h1] at h
    · simp [h0, h1] at h; exact .inr ⟨h0, h1, h.symm⟩

theorem mode_eq_observe {m : Mode} (h : m ≠ .modify) : m = .observe := by cases m <;> simp_all

theorem mem_descModes {s : S3} {a p : Nat} {m : Mode} :
    m ∈ descModes s a p ↔ ∃ j y, s.A[j]? = some y ∧ y.active = true ∧ p ∈ y.footprint ∧

content.content:
## 6. Arène : instance du modèle

L'arène est une abstraction possédant un stockage administré et une autorité interne sur ce stockage.

Son état logique comprend :

```text
Arena {
    anchor
    storage
    available
    issued
    internal_authority
}
```

### Invariant de l'arène

Les régions émises sont incluses dans le stockage administré.

Deux régions émises simultanément valides ne se chevauchent pas.

Les régions disponibles ne se chevauchent pas avec les régions encore distribuées.

Les accès distribués restent dépendants de l'ancre de l'arène.

### `arena.issue(region)`

**Préconditions**

- La région demandée est disponible.
- La région est disjointe des régions émises encore actives.
- L'abstraction dispose de l'autorité nécessaire pour distribuer cette région.
- Les métadonnées internes peuvent être modifiées conformément à leur discipline de mutation partagée ou intérieure.

**Effets**

- Retrait de la région de `available`.
- Création d'une autorité exclusive sur la région par séparation contrôlée.
- Ajout à `issued`.
- Association de l'autorité émise à l'ancre de l'arène.
- Préservation des régions déjà émises.

L'opération ne peut pas fabriquer une nouvelle autorité exclusive à partir d'une simple lecture ordinaire.

### `arena.reset()`

**Préconditions**

Aucune autorité émise encore active ni aucune valeur dépendante encore utilisable ne serait invalidée par la réinitialisation.

**Effets**

- Restitution des régions administrées à l'espace disponible.
- Invalidation des anciennes émissions selon le contrat de l'arène.
- Préservation des invariants de disjonction.

Le fait qu'une région ait été historiquement émise n'empêche pas éternellement sa récupération.

En revanche, une région encore effectivement utilisée ne peut être invalidée par `reset`.

### Propriétés attendues

- `arena_issue_preserves_disjointness`
- `arena_issue_keeps_earlier_blocks`
- `arena_reset_rejects_live_dependents`

/-- Preconditions of `arena.reset()` (MM-03.3 §6; A10): metadata right; no active authority
derived from `internal`; no usable place anchored on `internal` or on an authority derived from
it. -/
def ResetPre (k : K) (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (via : Nat) : Prop :=
  MetaRight k s ar via ∧
  (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, ar.internal ∈ s.ancs j → ¬ s.Active j) ∧
  (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, x ≠ ar.internal ∧ ar.internal ∉ s.ancs x)

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable] (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (via : Nat) :
    Decidable (ResetPre k s ar via) := by
  unfold ResetPre; infer_instance

/-- Effect of `arena.reset()` (MM-03.3 §6; A10): the whole storage becomes available, the past
emissions are forgotten, the metadata become `Init`. -/
def resetEff (s : S3) (ar : Arena) : S3 × Arena :=
  ({ s with I := fun l => if l ∈ metaLeaves s ar then .init else s.I l },
   { ar with available := s.afp ar.internal, issued := [] })

/-- `arena.reset` as a relation (MM-03.3 §6; A10). -/
def ResetStep (k : K) (ar : Arena) (via : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 (S3 × Arena) → Prop :=
  Guarded (ResetPre k s ar via) (resetEff s ar)
recorded arena, whose new logical state is written back; a missing entry is rejected. An entry
whose `internal` is released is rejected by `IssueStatic`, which asks it active. -/
inductive IssueAt (k : K) (i via : Nat) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) (s : S3) :
    AOutcome → Prop where
  | ok {ar : Arena} {s' : S3} {ar' : Arena} : s.arenas[i]? = some ar →
      IssueStep k ar via region dst s (.ok s' ar') → IssueAt k i via region dst s (.ok (arenaSet s' i ar'))
  | fail {ar : Arena} {s' : S3} {ar' : Arena} : s.arenas[i]? = some ar →
      IssueStep k ar via region dst s (.fail s' ar') → IssueAt k i via region dst s (.fail s)
  | reject {ar : Arena} : s.arenas[i]? = some ar → IssueStep k ar via region dst s .reject →
      IssueAt k i via region dst s .reject
  | none : s.arenas[i]? = none → IssueAt k i via region dst s .reject

/-- Preconditions of `arena.reset()` on the entry `i` of the state (MM-03.3 §6; A10; D3): the entry
exists and is live (an entry whose `internal` is released cannot be reset), and `ResetPre`. -/
def ResetAtPre (k : K) (s : S3) (i via : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.arenas[i]?) (fun ar => s.Active ar.internal ∧ ResetPre k s ar via) False

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable] (s : S3) (i via : Nat) :
    Decidable (ResetAtPre k s i via) := by
  unfold ResetAtPre; infer_instance

/-- Effect of `arena.reset()` on the entry `i` (D3): `resetEff`, the new logical state written
back. -/
def resetAtEff (s : S3) (i : Nat) : S3 :=
  match s.arenas[i]? with
  | some ar => arenaSet (resetEff s ar).1 i (resetEff s ar).2
  | none => s

/-- `arena.reset` on the entry `i` of the state as a relation (D3). -/
def ResetAtStep (k : K) (i via : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (ResetAtPre k s i via) (resetAtEff s i)

/-- Determinism of `newArena` (D3; F1). -/
theorem newArena_det {st i : Nat} {s : S3} {o₁ o₂ : Outcome3 S3} (h₁ : NewArenaStep st i s o₁)
    (h₂ : NewArenaStep st i s o₂) : o₁ = o₂ := Guarded.det h₁ h₂
